key_insight: A pseudostress-based fully mixed finite element method couples porous-solid deformation, fluid flow, electrostatics, and ionic transport while retaining stability near incompressibility.
engineering_relevance: The formulation supports simulation of charged, deformable porous media with direct flux approximations and algebraically reconstructed Cauchy stress.
method: Reformulate mechanics using non-symmetric pseudostress and displacement, with mixed Darcy, electrostatic, and ionic equations.
Discretize using conforming Raviart–Thomas elements and discontinuous polynomials.
Use a residual-based error estimator to guide adaptive refinement in two dimensions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports well-posedness and error estimates under stated assumptions, plus numerical tests of convergence, near-incompressibility robustness, adaptivity, and ionic polarization.
watch_item: Well-posedness requires block-stability and small-data assumptions; estimator reliability requires an additional smallness condition, and general boundary traces introduce oscillation terms.
paper_title: A pseudostress-based fully mixed finite element method for the stationary Biot--Poisson--Nernst--Planck system
